title: the class-2 PCRE branch now reads two fields from grep -n, matching its three sibling readers, so fence and ignore-marker suppression works on the GNU-grep branch CI takes

the commit hook still branches on any non-zero and still derives prefixes from paths it never checks resolve, so a staged initiative deletion exits 2 and blocks a clean commit; the exit-1-vs-exit-2 blocking semantics are still unsettled and CLAUDE.md now pins the unverified assumption
write_atomic with mktemp, directory-writability guard and EXIT/INT/TERM trap now backs all four formerly hand-rolled .tmp.$$ writers, and .gitignore covers every temp and lock name the code derives

stale-lock detection and trap save/restore both landed, but the flock branch still runs the locked body in a subshell while the mkdir branch runs it in the current shell, with the divergence documented nowhere

the three per-file guards landed but the per-initiative body is still unwrapped, so a die or non-zero rmw_state ends the sweep for every later initiative behind a hook that ends in || true; a state file whose .prefix mismatches its directory still creates a stray SRD directory

HANDOFF.md is now written atomically via write_atomic, but the notes filter still deletes every blank line and truncates at the first user heading, and the read-render-write is still unlocked so two concurrent checkpoints lose one window's notes
the open form of record-partial-verdict now nests an existing closed entry under prior instead of overwriting it, so the FAIL closure record survives a remediation re-open
the whole update-patterns read-dedup-insert-write is now inside with_state_lock on the pattern file, so two converging audits can no longer lose one another's insertion

both the grep -qxF pre-flight at :3778 and awk's $0 == h at :3647 are still fence-unaware and first-match-wins, so a pattern doc documenting its own Append Schema inside a fence gets the entry spliced into the fenced example and trips the blocking four-heading contract job

build_line_classes now records the opening fence run length and closes only on a run at least as long, emits an unterminated-fence diagnostic from END that is reported as a real violation, and strips CR in both awk bodies and all four snippet extractions

collect_md_files now has -type f, -print0 and an unreadable-file guard, but the class-4 line sets still ride in the environment with a || true consumer, so a large all-mermaid artifact can hit E2BIG and report zero findings indistinguishably from clean

the round number is now printed from inside the lock, double round completion is checked inside the lock, and cmd_init takes the lock -- but record-partial-verdict close is still pre-check-then-lock, so two concurrent closes both take the first-closure branch and the close-once invariant is violated silently

both token-read branches now use tolerant per-line jq -Rn with fromjson? and an unparseable attribution mode, and the fallback caps the concatenation rather than each file, so one torn line no longer collapses the scoped branch into the whole-directory sum

record_degraded_check is now idempotent on (check, reason) so degraded_checks no longer grows without bound, but gate-check still routes through rmw_state on every hook invocation for a legacy initiative -- taking the write lock, writing a .bak, and failing on a read-only checkout while its help text still says read-only

git_aware_mv now refuses an existing destination and treats a git mv failure on a tracked path as fatal, closing the nested SRD/.archived/PFX/PFX/ case that printed success and dropped all metrics history

eval:nightly now declares timeout: 150m, above the driver's 3 x 2700s phase budget plus provisioning, so the documented exit-4 / complete:false contract is reachable instead of being replaced by a GitLab timeout

an unparseable or zero-byte run.json still defaults to complete: true -- the guard at :521 coerces the unknown case to true rather than false -- so edm-compare-eval still compares a partial run against the baseline

the spliced pattern block has no terminating newline -- command substitution strips it at :3699 and _splice_pattern_file emits it with printf %s -- so the stub's last line fuses with the line at insert_line, swallowing the following ## heading whenever the target section has no trailing rule or blank

stale-lock reclamation is not atomic and mis-classifies live holders: the rm -rf between the kill -0 check and the mkdir can delete a lock another contender just took, kill -0 reports EPERM for a live cross-user holder as dead, and the reclaim paths continue without incrementing the retry bound

write_atomic installs a second trap layer inside with_state_lock's mkdir branch -- nesting depth two, which bin/tests/_harness.sh:49-50 documents as unsupported on bash 3.2 -- so a signal during the write leaks the lockdir, and an empty trap -p capture would re-disarm the outer cleanup CA-025 was filed to protect

the lock and write_atomic INT/TERM handlers clean up and then let execution resume, so a Ctrl-C inside the critical section releases the lock and keeps running the read-modify-write unlocked while another process can acquire it

an edm-lint-ignore marker on the line before a fence opener consumes the opener via ignore_next's next, so the fenced body is scanned as prose and the fence's closing line is then parsed as an opener, inverting suppression for the remainder of the file
